marta_engineer: Hey team — seeing a prod build failure after we published v2.3.0 of our TypeScript SDK. Next.js SSR build fails with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED when consumers import deep subpaths (e.g. `@our/sdk/lib/foo`).

marta_engineer: Repro is small and deterministic. Consumers on Next 13/14 and Rollup/Vite show same error in server builds. Here is the package.json exports we shipped:

```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
  },
  "./lib/*": "./dist/lib/*.js"
},
"main": "dist/index.cjs",
"module": "dist/index.mjs",
"types": "dist/index.d.ts"
```

marta_engineer: Build log excerpt:
```
Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: No "exports" main defined for package "@our/sdk" at Object.resolve (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:...)
    at Module._resolveFilename (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:...)
    at Function.resolve (internal/modules/helpers:...)
    at server (/vercel/0/node_modules/next/dist/server/require.js:...)
```

erin_support: Oof. Can you paste Node, npm, and TS versions + a link to a minimal repro (or attach a zip)? Also which bundlers/hosts affected (Next/Vercel, Rollup, Vite)?

marta_engineer: Node 18.17.1, npm 9.6, TS 5.1.0. A private repro repo is attached to ticket SUP-4521 (I can share access). A minimal reproduction shows imports like `import { foo } from "@our/sdk/lib/foo"` failing at runtime.

james_devx: This is a classic exports map vs TypeScript types resolution mismatch. Key points:
- Node's exports map controls runtime resolution for consumers; TS's resolver relies on "types"/"typesVersions" or on package entrypoints, not on the exports map for deep paths.
- If you export deep subpaths ("./lib/*"), you must publish the corresponding .d.ts files at the same paths (e.g. dist/lib/foo.d.ts), or TypeScript consumers will fail to find types and some bundlers may fall back to unexpected resolution.

james_devx: Quick workarounds to try now:
1) Publish matching type files for deep paths. Ensure the tarball includes dist/lib/*.d.ts.
2) Add explicit top-level exports and discourage deep imports: only support `@our/sdk` root entry (export public api there).
3) For consumers using Next/Vercel, add the package to `transpilePackages` or configure bundler to handle mixed ESM/CJS.

james_devx: Example package.json recommended layout (JS + types):
```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
  },
  "./lib/*": "./dist/lib/*.js"
},
"main": "dist/index.cjs",
"module": "dist/index.mjs",
"types": "dist/index.d.ts"
```
Note: TypeScript will look at "types" for the main entrypoint; it won't automatically use the exports map to locate deep .d.ts unless those files exist at the deep paths.

james_devx: For Rollup/Vite/Next bundlers you can also: add `optimizeDeps.exclude` (Vite) or `transpilePackages` (Next) to avoid automatic ESM->CJS transforms on our package, or set `build.commonjsOptions.transformMixedEsModules: true` when using SWC/commonjs.

marta_engineer: We tried adding `types: dist/index.d.ts` but consumers still error when they do deep imports. They rely on `@our/sdk/lib/foo` not `@our/sdk`. Is there a way to map .d.ts files for deep exports?

james_devx: Yes — you must publish the .d.ts files at the matching deep paths (dist/lib/foo.d.ts). If you cannot publish them, you can add a small compatibility index that re-exports everything from the main entry and update docs to import from root. Another option is `typesVersions` in package.json to guide TS for subpath mappings, e.g.:
```
"typesVersions": {
  "*": {
    "lib/*": ["dist/lib/*"]
  }
}
```
But that is brittle and requires consumers' TS to honor it.

erin_support: I've escalated to eng-packaging and eng-runtime. Please `npm pack` locally and paste the file list (we want to confirm whether dist/*.d.ts are present in the published tarball). Also attach your published package sha so we can inspect the npm registry package contents.

marta_engineer: Will run `npm pack` and attach results to SUP-4521. For now we reverted to v2.2.8 in production. Thanks for the quick triage.

deploy-bot: Notice: Reverted @our/sdk to v2.2.8 on prod at 2026-03-16T18:02:00Z :rocket:

james_devx: Long-term we should add a CI check: after build, run `npm pack --dry-run` or `tar -tf` and assert every export path has a corresponding .d.ts (or add a test to ensure no ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED on a Node 18 clean install). I can draft a PR with a test script.

marta_engineer: Thanks — appreciated. @erin_support I'll DM the repro link and the tarball when `npm pack` output is ready.
